- none found in the notes

### Variables
- none. There is no `.env.example` content provided (file appears empty), and this release introduces no new or renamed provider configuration variables. - none. No database, cache, or other companion service version is named anywhere in these notes.

## Upstream changes 26.8.1 -> 26.8.2

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — this is a large security patch (34 CVEs, several unauthenticated DoS/account-takeover issues, one reproduced against 26.8.1 itself) and the image upgrades its embedded Quarkus runtime, but nothing in the notes or the image diff requires a config change or manual migration.

### Breaking changes
- None found in the notes. The only behavioural item called out is `#54184 Upgrade to Quarkus 3.40.1.1`, which is an internal runtime bump, not a documented breaking change.
- No UPGRADING/BREAKING_CHANGES/CHANGELOG section was supplied for this range — only the generic boilerplate "Before upgrading refer to the migration guide" appears in both the 26.8.2 and 26.8.1 notes. Treat the upstream migration guide as unread; if the operator wants certainty beyond what's quoted here, it should be checked by hand at https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/upgrading/#migration-changes.

### Variables
- None. No variable renames, removals, or new requirements appear in the notes, and the compose file / .env.example need no edits for this range.

### Data and dependencies
- None introduced by this range. The notes mention a MySQL/MariaDB-specific fix (`#54687`, login-failure upsert trusting affected-row count) and an Infinispan cache-contention fix (`#53809`), but these are code-level fixes with no stated version floor or migration step — this template runs Postgres, not MySQL/MariaDB, so `#54687` does not apply to this deployment.
- Companion service versions: the compose file pins `postgres:16` for the database. Nothing in the 26.8.2 notes names a required Postgres version this pin fails to meet, so this does not block the verdict.

### Before applying
- Take the routine backup before any Keycloak upgrade (the `backups` sidecar already runs continuously, but confirm a recent dump exists before pulling the new image, given the volume of auth/session-handling fixes in this release).
- No manual migration command or config edit is indicated by the notes.
- Because several fixes touch active sessions, SSO note handling and broker/IdP linking (`#54688`, `#54707`, `#53634`), expect that upgrading will invalidate some in-flight sessions tied to the patched flows — plan the restart for a low-traffic window.

### Notes read
- `26.8.2` (2026-11-05) — full release notes as supplied.
- `26.8.1` (2026-10-13) — supplied as baseline only, used to confirm which items are new to this range.
- No UPGRADING / BREAKING_CHANGES / CHANGELOG document was provided beyond the "see migration guide" pointer in both release notes; the migration guide itself was not supplied and was not read.
